column1: # Game profile of Castlevania: Belmont's Curse (Switch, update 1.1.0 = v65536). Plays on the Mac
# Format: see dm/games/README.md; bring-up and measurements in README.md beside this file

# Unity 2022.3.62f2 (IL2CPP) with FMOD, SDK 19.3.16, NVN; subsdk0 is the movie module, which plays the opening movie (MP4s inside the narration-videos bundles). The shaders are Unity's Shader and ComputeShader objects in the player's serialized files and the StreamingAssets bundles, read by unityfs.py, and the player's 11 GLSLC outputs in main.
# The game asks for present interval 1 and runs at 60 fps. Docked (1920x1080) with the 2D pad layout: B jumps, Y attacks

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true: nninitStartup hands application pool − used memory to StandardAllocator as one address region
# (it returns to main+0xca8c0c) and never calls SetMemoryHeapSize. The SDK-wide node area cut applies (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py MATCH_CUTS, implementation 5).
# The layout of Cult of the Lamb, the same Unity generation: a 1 GB pool and the 5 GB block (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region).
# With the hardware pool the heap check's alias region reached +4.25 GB within two seconds. With 1 GB: +3.50 GB in play, 1.75 GB mapped
# The game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode(near = 0) (log: "depth mode near=0"), so its vertex shaders use the main0_z entries; the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader and ComputeShader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# everything is under Data/: the player's serialized files and the StreamingAssets bundles
